searchText: <@!543900561460822016> <@!153709109122826240> and I will be working here on getting mev-boost milestone 1 tested with mergemock gm What is the argument for CL calling a builder with `engine_forkChoiceUpdated` vs. something like `builder_preparePayload` that just includes the required attributes and head hash to build on? no particular reason, it's a vestige of how mev-boost used to be a middleware <@153709109122826240> <@543900561460822016> https://github.com/realbigsean/mock-relay This is <@607055410104500244> 's testing relay. I think the argument for keeping it is that the relay will have to inevitably do the same operations that an execution client would Shouldn’t a relay be running their own CL though? hmm true, it will be running both an execution and consensus client if we go further down this road, I'd almost prefer to do away with the `preparePayload` call completely, since it actually adds little value to the relay Right, so maybe it makes sense to have a single method `getPayload` that’s takes a block hash as a parameter and then relay returns a header built on top of that block? yep the eventual plan is that relays should be building blocks pre-emptively across many likely block head states, so it should be ready to reply with a header almost immediately in any case

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: What is the argument for CL calling a builder with `engine_forkChoiceUpdated` vs. something like `builder_preparePayload` that just includes the required attributes and head hash to build on?

excerpts.author: ranisis
excerpts.content: no particular reason, it's a vestige of how mev-boost used to be a middleware

excerpts.author: ranisis
excerpts.content: I think the argument for keeping it is that the relay will have to inevitably do the same operations that an execution client would

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: Shouldn’t a relay be running their own CL though?

excerpts.author: ranisis
excerpts.content: hmm true, it will be running both an execution and consensus client
